title: A failed /(?{})/ branch restores a COW-backed subbeg without its length, so $& reads past the match
live_proof: upstream fixed it in af11b0c528 (af11b0c528200761891d46a7f6566aa880be45ca) (2026-07-03). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin regexec.c:10978 eval_state->subbeg = NULL; regexec.c:11010 unconditional RXp_MATCH_COPIED_on(rex); regexp.h:648 has no subbeg_flags). Host ASan at the pin: no ASan report; the workload's own oracle fails (rc=0); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sysalloc-sublet.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sublet-svheads.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: no report: completes; with revocation off (_RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1) the same binary gives: no report: completes

status: all three Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
allocator_layer: system allocator (the RXp_SUBBEG buffer), plus the nested SV head arena (saved_copy)
note: triggered on every arm, on both platforms, and catchable by NONE of them, for a structural reason worth recording: the stale subbeg length makes $& read one byte past the logical string into the NUL terminator, which lies INSIDE the same allocation. No per-object bounds and no revocation can see an in-bounds read of a live object -- CheriBSD with revocation on is clean here too. The only oracle is the wrong output, which every arm does produce
